habitat.typical_environment: Burrows deeply in sand, mud, sandy mud and sandy gravel, particularly in estuaries and tidal flats.

edibility_and_safety.edibility: Edible and commercially harvested.
edibility_and_safety.safety_warning: Consume only softshell clams from approved and monitored harvesting areas because they can accumulate marine biotoxins and pollutants.
edibility_and_safety.toxicity: Not inherently toxic; contaminated individuals can carry harmful microorganisms or marine biotoxins.
edibility_and_safety.human_consumption: Commonly harvested as a food shellfish.

appearance.shell_shape: Large, fan-shaped scallop shell with rounded margins and prominent hinge ears.
appearance.shell_color: Upper valve commonly reddish, pinkish, brown or orange; lower valve generally pale or cream.
appearance.pattern: Radial sculpture and variable bands or blotches may occur on the shell surface.
appearance.surface_texture: Fan-shaped shell with radial ribs and growth lines; generally smoother than heavily ribbed scallop species.
appearance.size: Up to approximately 17 cm shell diameter; commonly 10–15 cm.
appearance.distinctive_markings: Large fan-shaped outline, prominent hinge ears and contrasting upper and lower valves.

habitat.habitat_type: Continental shelf and coastal seabed
habitat.geographic_distribution: Eastern Atlantic and Mediterranean Sea.
habitat.typical_environment: Benthic seabeds where it can swim using rapid opening and closing of its valves; suspension feeder.

edibility_and_safety.edibility: Edible and commercially important scallop.
edibility_and_safety.safety_warning: Consume only scallops obtained from regulated sources because shellfish can accumulate marine biotoxins and pollutants.
edibility_and_safety.toxicity: Not inherently toxic, but contamination and harmful algal blooms may make scallops unsafe.
edibility_and_safety.human_consumption: Widely consumed as a food species, particularly its adductor muscle.

appearance.shell_shape: Large, nearly circular fan-shaped shell with two valves and prominent hinge ears.
appearance.shell_color: Upper valve commonly reddish-brown, pink, orange or darker shades; lower valve generally white or cream.
appearance.pattern: Usually shows fine radial sculpture and variable coloration across the upper valve.
appearance.surface_texture: Relatively smooth compared with strongly ribbed scallops, with fine growth lines.
appearance.size: Up to approximately 20 cm shell diameter.
appearance.distinctive_markings: Large circular fan-shaped shell, broad hinge ears and relatively smooth shell surface.

habitat.habitat_type: Continental shelf benthic habitat
habitat.geographic_distribution: Northwest Atlantic, from the Strait of Belle Isle in Canada southward to Georges Bank and Cape Hatteras, North Carolina.
habitat.typical_environment: Large epibenthic populations on continental-shelf sediments; semi-mobile and capable of swimming.

edibility_and_safety.edibility: Edible and commercially important seafood species.
edibility_and_safety.safety_warning: Consume only scallops from regulated harvesting areas because shellfish may accumulate marine biotoxins and contaminants.
edibility_and_safety.toxicity: Not inherently toxic; food safety depends on harvesting conditions and proper handling.
edibility_and_safety.human_consumption: The adductor muscle is widely harvested and consumed.

appearance.shell_shape: Thick, solid, strongly inflated and broadly ovate shell with nearly equal valves.
appearance.shell_color: White beneath a yellowish-brown to brown periostracum.
appearance.pattern: Approximately 15–20 prominent radial ribs with regularly arranged nodules.
appearance.surface_texture: Strongly rugose radial ribs with nodules and crenulated internal shell margins.
appearance.size: Up to approximately 9 cm shell length; commonly around 6 cm.
appearance.distinctive_markings: Strongly inflated shell, prominent umbones, roughly 18 nodular radial ribs and strongly crenulated inner margins.

habitat.habitat_type: Intertidal and shallow estuarine habitat
habitat.geographic_distribution: Indo-Pacific, from eastern Africa and India through Southeast Asia, Japan, Australia and Polynesia.
habitat.typical_environment: Muddy bottoms of protected bays, estuaries and mangrove areas; commonly found in silty low-salinity intertidal habitats.

edibility_and_safety.edibility: Edible and commercially important food shellfish.
edibility_and_safety.safety_warning: Blood cockles should only be consumed when legally harvested and properly processed because bivalves can accumulate pathogens, marine biotoxins and pollutants.
edibility_and_safety.toxicity: Not inherently toxic, but raw or contaminated cockles can present significant food-safety risks.
edibility_and_safety.human_consumption: Widely harvested and cultured for human consumption throughout parts of the Indo-Pacific.

appearance.shell_color: Natural outer coloration including brown, white, cream, greenish, or patterned hues.
appearance.pattern: Radial ribs, concentric growth ridges, or natural periostracum layers.

appearance.size: Varies by species; small to large marine and estuarine bivalve.
